clue.text: Small person's wife going into spasm

indicators.note: going into tells us one piece is placed inside the other here

parts.note: a titch is a very small person (British informal)

explanation.surface: A little man's wife suddenly has a fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going into' puts W inside TITCH, the British slang word for a very small person.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitch is a sudden involuntary jerk of a muscle, which is what a spasm is.

clue.text: Pierce through vehicles I left for repair

indicators.note: left as in departed, so the letter I is taken away

parts.note: trains are vehicles running on rails
to fix something is to repair it

explanation.surface: Instructions to puncture some vehicles, having left them in for repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes I from TRAINS to give TRANS, then FIX is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfix is literally to impale something, driving a point right through it.

clue.text: No aides in developing country

indicators.note: developing suggests the letters are changing into a new form

explanation.surface: A developing country is short of aid workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a large island nation in South-East Asia.

clue.text: He will investigate if anyone is unusually late

definitions.text: He will investigate if anyone is unusually late

parts.words: He will investigate if anyone is unusually late
parts.note: late here means dead, so an official looks into deaths that are not natural

explanation.surface: A man who checks up whenever someone turns up late.
explanation.definitionFit: This official holds inquests into sudden or suspicious deaths.

clue.text: How healthy pig will go the full extent?

parts.note: whole in its old sense means sound and healthy
a hog is a pig

explanation.surface: A question about how far a fit pig will travel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface leans on the idiom 'go the whole hog', meaning to do something completely; 'How ... will go' is link padding round it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom about going all the way, this phrase stands for everything, the complete amount.

clue.text: Hating research about examination of one's deepest feelings

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who loathes research reflects on their inner self.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart-searching is close scrutiny of one's own motives and emotions.

clue.text: Heraldic beast, once ill, sickens

indicators.note: sickens suggests the letters fall into a disordered state

explanation.surface: A creature on a coat of arms, once unwell, gets worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A lioncel is a small lion shown on a coat of arms, a heraldic creature.

clue.text: Lift to interminable place of happiness

indicators.note: interminable here means without an end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: heaven is a place of perfect bliss

explanation.surface: Being raised up to an everlasting paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminable' removes the last letter N from HEAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to raise something heavy with effort, so it is a lift.

clue.text: In spring Dan skied in Poland

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is contained within the following words

explanation.surface: Dan went skiing in Poland during the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in sprinG DAN SKied. The definition reads as 'a place in Poland'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gdansk is a port city on Poland's Baltic coast.

clue.text: Union members celebrate it after over half a century

definitions.text: Union members celebrate it after over half a century

parts.words: Union members celebrate it after over half a century
parts.note: the union is a marriage, and its partners mark sixty years together

explanation.surface: Trade unionists hold a party for a long-serving anniversary.
explanation.definitionFit: This anniversary marks sixty years of marriage.

clue.text: Not starting to be less hairy tree!

indicators.note: not starting tells us the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: balder means having less hair

explanation.surface: A tree is apparently going bald.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not starting' removes the B from BALDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a common waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: Lover in foreign capital returning a word of thanks

indicators.note: returning means the city's name is read backwards

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name for Rome, a capital city
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A lover abroad in a capital sends back a thank-you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ROMA into AMOR. TA is everyday British slang for 'thanks'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman with whom one is in love, a female sweetheart.

clue.text: Term very much like another

parts.note: a word whose meaning closely matches that of a different word

explanation.surface: A description of a word that closely resembles a second one.
explanation.definitionFit: A word sharing its meaning with a different word is exactly what this grammatical label names.

clue.text: Watches initial part of poster be put at the end

indicators.note: initial part of picks out the opening letter of the word for poster
be put at the end tells us that letter is moved to the back

parts.note: a sticker is a small poster or label stuck up for display

explanation.surface: Someone watches as a poster's first bit is moved to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter S of STICKER moves to the end. 'Watches' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickers is slang for watches and clocks, from the ticking sound they make.

clue.text: Policy is to ask for money — at a premium?

definitions.text: Policy is to ask for money — at a premium?

parts.words: Policy is to ask for money — at a premium?
parts.note: a demand for payment made under an insurance policy, on which premiums have been paid

explanation.surface: Someone's guiding principle is always to ask for money at a high price.
explanation.definitionFit: A demand made to an insurer for payment under a policy for which premiums were paid.

clue.text: Dish causing turmoil in the emerald isle?

parts.note: the Emerald Isle is a name for Ireland
a stew is a state of agitation or turmoil

explanation.surface: A meal that causes chaos in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' is a link; STEW (a state of worry) is qualified by IRISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish stew is a traditional dish of mutton, potatoes and onions.

clue.text: Lawyer's power?

parts.note: a legal document called a power of the agent named in it

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase power of attorney names legal authority to act for another; in the US this word also means a lawyer.

clue.text: Cover used during one's retirement designed piecemeal

definitions.text: Cover used during one's retirement designed piecemeal

parts.words: Cover used during one's retirement designed piecemeal
parts.note: a bedcover used when one retires to bed, made by sewing pieces together

explanation.surface: Something to keep a pensioner covered in old age, put together bit by bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests leaving work, but here it means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedspread sewn from many small scraps of fabric, the cover one sleeps under.

clue.text: Band opposing Ronald, revolutionary leader

parts.note: Che Guevara was a revolutionary leader
v, short for versus, means opposing
Ron is short for Ronald

explanation.surface: A music group sets itself against Ronald, a rebel leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is a V-shaped stripe, a band on a sleeve or heraldic shield.

clue.text: Queen on river did not start to argue over petty things

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second
did not start means the first letter is removed

parts.note: the Ribble is a river in north-west England

explanation.surface: A queen on a river would not set off, choosing to bicker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did not start' takes R off RIBBLE, the river in Lancashire, leaving IBBLE under QU.
explanation.definitionFit: To quibble is to raise trivial objections, nit-picking about minor matters.

clue.text: Smear be over a bud developing

indicators.note: developing suggests the letters grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener daubs over a bud that is opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges BE and A BUD together.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedaub is to smear something messily, to plaster it.

clue.text: Find Lee struggling in the London area

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Track down Lee, who is having a hard time somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges the letters of FIND LEE. ENFIELD is a borough in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Enfield is a north London borough, a district of the capital.

clue.text: Fellow with daughter accepted one resisted

indicators.note: accepted means the outer letters take the other piece in

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A man and his daughter took in one and stood up to opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted' puts ACE inside F and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To have faced something is to have confronted and stood up to it.

clue.text: Rachel flint's middle name, we hear — oh, well!

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: Rachel Heyhoe Flint was a famous England women's cricket captain

explanation.surface: Musing on a cricketer's middle name, then sighing resignedly.
explanation.walkthrough: Rachel Heyhoe Flint captained England's women cricketers; her middle name HEYHOE sounds like the sighing exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation expresses weary resignation or boredom, like a sigh.

clue.text: Musical folder?

parts.note: an instrument whose bellows fold up and open out as it is played

explanation.definitionFit: This squeezebox instrument works by its pleated bellows folding and unfolding, so it is a musical thing that folds.

clue.text: Club may charge

parts.note: a police club or truncheon, used in a charge by officers

explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a club, and police using them rush a crowd in a so-called charge with it.

clue.text: A beading removed whilst producing banter

indicators.note: removed in the sense of moved again, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: A decorative beading was taken away amid playful chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' rearranges the letters of A BEADING.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light-hearted teasing conversation, which is banter.

clue.text: Main trade route

parts.note: a principal route for trade, with main also hinting at the open sea

explanation.definitionFit: An ocean-going channel such as the St Lawrence one carries commercial shipping, a trading lane for vessels.
